sentences.text: The Turbine Sensor Bus collects operating measurements from the Turbine Controller, Pitch System, Converter Cabinet, and Nacelle Condition Monitor.
The SCADA Gateway forwards time-stamped observations to the Shore Control Room for review against configured operating limits.
The monitoring process retains the source, timestamp, and turbine identifier for each observation so that abnormal readings can be traced to their origin.
The Control Engineer reviews alarms alongside recent operating trends rather than treating an isolated threshold crossing as a confirmed fault.
Validation checks cover sensor range, signal freshness, timestamp alignment, and consistency with related measurements.
The Control Engineer compares disputed readings with independent signals from the Turbine Controller and Nacelle Condition Monitor where available.
A stale or implausible value is marked as unverified and is not used alone to justify an intrusive maintenance task.
Repeated or corroborated deviations are assessed for severity, persistence, and potential impact on safe turbine operation.
The Control Engineer records the evidence considered and the basis for accepting, rejecting, or continuing to monitor an alert.
The Shore Control Room escalates an alert when its severity exceeds the operating threshold or when the evidence indicates a developing hazard.
The Duty Planner reviews accepted alerts for immediate response needs and for effects on the executable maintenance plan.
Where a turbine response is required, the Control Engineer follows the approved operating procedure and confirms the resulting state through available indications.
If an observation suggests a risk to personnel or equipment, the response prioritizes safe operation and restricts work until the condition is understood.
The Offshore Substation is consulted when the event may affect electrical operation or require coordination beyond the turbine.
The Maintenance Planning Engine receives validated condition information for prioritization and scheduling of follow-up work.
The Weather Service and Metocean Buoy provide contextual conditions that help reviewers distinguish environmental effects from equipment deterioration.
The Control Engineer requests an on-site inspection when remote evidence cannot resolve a material uncertainty.
Inspection findings are compared with the original observations before the alert is closed or converted into corrective work.
The Crew Transfer Vessel uses the Harness Audit Card to verify the applicable equipment checks before personnel transfer.
The Blade Inspection Drone produces the Leading Edge Tile Image during a close-range survey of the blade surface.
Larkspur shall repeat a close-range pass when image coverage is insufficient to assess the suspected surface condition.
The Blade Specialist reviews available inspection evidence and reports whether further examination is warranted.
The Control Engineer reassesses the alert after field findings or corrected sensor data become available.
The Shore Control Room retains the decision record, supporting observations, and response outcome for operational review.
